newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-JAYASURIYA, MAHANAMA IN RECORD PARTNERSHIP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JAYASURIYA, MAHANAMA IN RECORD PARTNERSHIP.

text.p: A record second wicket partnership between Sri Lankans Sanath Jayasuriya and Roshan Mahanama on Monday virtually guaranteed the first test against India will be drawn.

Replying to India's mammoth first innings of 537 for eight declared, Jayasuriya and Mahanama took advantage of a lifeless pitch to bat right through the third day, posting individual centuries as well as Sri Lanka's highest partnership in test cricket.

By the close, Jayasuriya had reached his best test score of 175 not out and Mahanama was on 115. Their unbroken stand of 283 left Sri Lanka in relative safety on 322 for one, just 16 short of avoiding the follow-on.
Jayasuriya led the way with some exciting strokeplay which brought him 14 boundaries as he raced to his century from just 138 balls.

He reached his third test century in fine style, moving from 85 to 101 in five scoring strokes including three successive fours as he took 16 runs off test debutant Nilesh Kulkarni, who had taken a wicket with his first ball in test cricket on Sunday.
Jayasuriya slowed a little after tea but passed 150 for the first time in test cricket and at the close had been at the crease just under seven hours. He faced 299 balls and hit 20 fours

Mahanama, playing the supporting role, completed his fourth test century in 44 tests, and his first for four years, when he pulled a short delivery from Venkatesh Prasad for his 12th four. It came in 345 minutes and he faced 244 balls.
When he reached 109, however, Mahanama gave the only chance of the day when he stepped out to drive off-spinner Chetan Chauhan and edged the ball past Indian wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia.
Their partnership was also the highest-ever in a Sri Lanka-India test, beating the 272 for the sixth wicket between Mohammad Azharuddin and Kapil Dev at Kanpur in 1986-87.

It was also only the second time a Sri Lankan pair had batted through an entire day following the previous record stand of 240 between Asanka Gurusinha and Arjuna Ranatunga for the fourth wicket against Pakistan in 1985-86.
